dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Lines assume no man in the party.

say: A woman on this road with no man beside her. Explain yourself, or explain it to the Inquisitors.
Where's your escort? The Flame doesn't look kindly on a woman walking alone.
No brother, no husband. Those who walk alone are marked as tainted. Which are you?
Keep your head down and your business short. Women don't wander here unattended.
You are far from a man's roof. That is how the Inquisitorium finds its work.
I have no quarrel with you yet. See that I never do. Find a man to walk behind.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Lines assume no man in the party.

say: The Inquisitorium keeps no women, and wants none. Be gone before somebody writes your name down.
A woman, unescorted. Seta would have words. I'd rather not repeat them to you.
Tainted ones come in two kinds. Those who know it, and those about to be told.
Whose are you? Somebody must answer for you, or the Flame will.
I see no master at your side. The law has a name for that, and a punishment.
Leave. If I must ask twice, I will not ask.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Lines assume no man in the party.

say: Daughter, a woman alone is a door left open. Close it. Go home, and pray.
Narko whispers to the unattended. Have you no one to speak for you, child?
You walk without a man at your shoulder. The Lord of Light sees that.
Humility, sister. Cover yourself and keep to a man's side.
A woman out alone is the most dangerous thing in the Nation.
Pray, and go home. I will pretend I did not see you, this once.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Lines assume no man in the party.

say: Halt. No woman passes unescorted. Fetch a husband or a brother, or turn around.
A woman needs a male escort in this city. You have none.
Not without a man to answer for you. Those are the rules, and the rules are the wall.
Come back with a man at your side. Until then you are not getting past me.
Unescorted women are punished here. I'm doing you a kindness by saying no.
Do not argue. A woman who argues with a guard is a woman on the way to the cells.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Assumes a man travels with her.

say: You there. Is she yours? Then keep her at your side, and keep her quiet.
I'll speak to you, not her. Is this woman in your charge?
Brother, a woman in your care is your sin if she strays.
Good. A man with her. See she stays behind you.
Her conduct is your responsibility. I hope you take it seriously.
I ask the man. The woman need not trouble herself to answer.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Assumes a man travels with her.

say: Speak for her. If she's yours, say so. If she isn't, say so faster.
A woman needs a man to answer for her. Are you he, or must I find another?
The Inquisitorium looks to the man. Whatever she does, you will answer for.
Keep her close. Tainted women are cured by discipline, not by freedom.
Is she obedient? Don't tell me. Show me, by keeping her silent.
I am watching her. You should be, too. One of us is paid for it.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Assumes a man travels with her.

say: Brother, guide her gently, and firmly. A woman without guidance is easily led astray.
Bless you for walking with her. A wandering woman is a burden on her keeper's soul.
Does she pray? A man should know. He is answerable for it.
I'll address you, brother. She's welcome to listen.
Keep her from temptation, and yourself from hers. That's the whole law.
Walk ahead of her. A man leads. The Lord of Light was clear on it.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Assumes a man travels with her.

say: She goes where you go, and says what you let her. That is the arrangement.
Is the woman yours? Then she passes behind you.
Talk to me, not to her. Are you her escort?
Mind her. If she misbehaves in the city, you will pay.
A man with her is the only reason I am being polite. Keep it that way.
Keep her close, keep her modest, and keep moving.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Assumes women travel with the man.

say: Those women are yours? Then their sins are yours, brother.
I see you travel with women. Wise, to keep them near. Wiser still to keep them quiet.
Are they your wives, or your trouble? Either way, you answer for them.
A man's women are his duty. Do not let them wander from your sight.
Control your women and we'll have no business, you and I.
Your women are not my concern, so long as they are yours. Make sure they remain so.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Assumes women travel with the man.

say: Whose are the women? Yours? Then the Inquisitorium looks to you if they stray.
A man with women in tow. Keep them leashed, in word and in habit.
Tell me they're obedient. Then prove it by their silence.
I won't bother them. I'll bother you, if they give cause.
You answer for each one. Every word, every glance.
Women are nearly always trouble. Yours had better be the exception.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Assumes women travel with the man.

say: Brother, you carry a heavy charge. Women need guidance, and you're the guide.
Bless you for shepherding them. Keep them from the temptations of the road.
Do they pray as they should? A man ought to know.
Keep them at your back and your faith at your front.
The Lord of Light gave them to men for a reason.
A good man guides his women. A fool loses them.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Assumes women travel with the man.

say: Your women stay behind you in the city. Remember it, and we will agree.
Keep your women quiet and out of the way. Pass.
You answer for them while you are in the city. Every one of them.
If any of them wanders off alone, you're the one who pays.
Women follow the man. That is how it is done here. Do it that way.
I would rather not deal with any of them. Make sure I never have to.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Also DC_IM_UNARMED (target, value 0).

say: A blade on a woman. Moll's kind carry steel. Which kind are you?
Put that away before it's taken. A woman with a sword is a heresy with a handle.
Armed, and no man to answer for you. That's two crimes before I have asked a question.
Who gave you that blade? A woman has no use for one, only an excuse.
Don't touch it. I'd so hate to have to be sure of you.
The Nation has burned women for less than a sword.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Also DC_IM_UNARMED (target, value 0).

say: Steel in a woman's hand. A confession in waiting, I think.
Women who bear arms tend to follow the one who calls herself Moll. Do you?
Take no offence. I only wish to know whether to arrest you or merely watch you.
Armed and alone. The file almost writes itself.
A woman's weapon is her obedience. Where is yours?
The sword gives away what your face hides. Set it down, or explain it.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Also DC_IM_UNARMED (target, value 0).

say: Weapons are for men. Hand it over or turn around.
A woman with a sword gets no welcome here. Sheath it, and keep walking.
Not escorted, and armed. You manage both. Impressive.
Do not make me ask whose blade that is. I will not like the answers.
Keep that sheathed. The cells are full of women who did not.
We have no use for fighting women. Move along.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Also DC_IS_SNEAKING (target).

say: Creeping. A woman with something to hide, or someone to hide from. Which is it?
Step into the light, woman. Honest people don't crouch.
I saw that. A woman skulking along a wall is nothing the Flame needs explained.
Stand up. Slowly. Tell me who you're escaping.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Also DC_IS_SNEAKING (target).

say: A woman who creeps is a woman who has been told not to.
Skulking and unescorted. I'll remember your face.
The innocent walk straight. You don't.
Hiding from whom, woman? From us, or from yourself?

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Also DC_IS_SNEAKING (target).

say: Stop right there. Honest women do not creep around a wall.
Sneaking in the Nation. A woman. You'll want to explain that to someone else.
Come out where I can see you. The sooner, the shorter the questions.
I see you. Don't run. The ones who run are the ones we remember.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Also DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target); relies on the engine's own test.

say: Forbidden things in a woman's pack. Narko's work, plainly.
Women should not carry what men dare not. Open the bag.
Darkness smells the same in any hand. In yours it smells worse.
A tainted woman and tainted goods. You've made my morning simple.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Also DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target); relies on the engine's own test.

say: Forbidden goods, and a woman to carry them. I couldn't have designed it better.
Your pack is heresy. Your sex is merely the explanation.
The Inquisitorium has questions for the bag. It will have more for the woman.
Whose were these? You will name him, or take the blame whole.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Also DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target); relies on the engine's own test.

say: A woman carrying what the Lord forbids. Pray, daughter. Then open the bag.
Whatever is in there, it will not stay in your hands. Give it here, and kneel.
Narko has made you her porter. Set it down, and be forgiven the weight.
Temptation and contraband. Both end the same, in the Flame.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target), untested; fires only at an enemy player.

say: Tainted! A woman on the road with a price on her head! The Flame will have you!
Wicked daughter of Narko. Kneel, or burn standing.
No man, no leash, and no fear. That is how it begins.
Seize her! The Nation has no mercy for a wild woman!
You should have stayed behind a door. Doors are kinder than I am.
You dare walk in the Nation's sight? Your kind is not welcome here.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target), untested; fires only at an enemy player.

say: The Flame wants you. A woman. I'll take no pleasure.
Woman, you will be questioned. You will confess. That is the order of things.
Another tainted one, and an enemy besides.
Narko has led you astray. I will return you to the light, or to the ashes.
The Inquisitorium has a place for you.
You won't run, woman. Nobody does.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target), untested; fires only at an enemy player.

say: Repent, wretched woman! The Lord of Light sees all that you've done!
Narko's daughter, here in the open!
Even now you may kneel. Even now there is a lesser punishment.
You carry darkness in your very blood. Be cleansed.
The Flame purges what the Lord can't teach.
Temptress. Your day ends here.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target), untested; fires only at an enemy player.

say: A woman, wanted by the Nation! Alarm!
You! Stop! The Nation has no gate open for the likes of you!
Wild women are not tolerated here.
Alone and hunted. Foolish, tainted woman.
I won't be softened by a woman's tears.
Hands up! The law will deal with you.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target), untested; fires only when the Holy Nation is allied to the player.

say: You have the Nation's favour, woman. Do not mistake it for freedom.
Allies are allies. Still, a woman should walk with a man, even a friend of the Flame.
I won't trouble you. Others may, and I can't stop them all.
You've done the Nation service. Keep your head covered and your voice low, and few will complain.
The paladins remember good service. The Inquisitors remember everything else.
Peace to you, sister. Walk carefully.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target), untested; fires only when the Holy Nation is allied to the player.

say: The Nation's friend, and a woman. A rare combination. I shall note it, kindly.
Your deeds are written. So is your sex. Both matter to the Inquisitorium.
Don't let your service make you proud. Pride is a woman's first sin.
You have friends in high places, for now. Keep them, and keep your silence.
Be careful whom you speak to. Not all of us read the same page about you.
I won't question you today.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target), untested; fires only when the Holy Nation is allied to the player.

say: Bless you for your service, daughter. May it earn your soul some quiet.
The Lord of Light rewards humility. See that you show some.
You've been a friend to the Nation. That counts, even for a woman.
Walk in the light, sister, and keep close to those who guide you.
Your faith is noted. Your freedom, less so.
The Flame keeps its friends. It keeps everyone else, too.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target), untested; fires only when the Holy Nation is allied to the player.

say: You may pass. A friend of the Nation does not need a husband. Not today.
Allied, aye. Still, keep to the main road and keep your head down.
I won't stop you. I might wish I had, if the Inquisitors ask.
The Nation vouches for you. I do, a little.
You know the rules. I need not repeat them.
Pass, and do not linger.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Fires only at an enemy player.

say: Heretic, and with women in tow. The Flame will have them too.
You answer for them, and you answer to me.
A man who drags women into his crimes is twice a sinner.
You will die first. Your women will watch. Then they will be taken in hand.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE (target) and DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), both untested in game; assumes the flag describes the player's squad. Fires only at an enemy player.

say: A heretic with a household of tainted women. The Inquisitorium thanks you for your trouble.
You corrupt them, and then you bring them near the holy ones. Shameless.
Whatever they have done, you are the one who answers.
Your women will be questioned. You, I'll only kill.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE / DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), untested. Lore basis: refugees afraid of Holy Nation spies, ninjas calling each other sister.

say: Sister. Good. Keep walking, nobody here will ask where you came from.
You walk like someone who has done it alone. Come in from the road if you want.
A woman on the road. Eat something before you leave. That's the whole rule.
We know the look. Take your time, and we won't ask for a story.
The Nation hasn't broken everything. You're proof.
Stay as long as you can pay for it. Otherwise you're welcome.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE / DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), untested. Lore basis: refugees afraid of Holy Nation spies, ninjas calling each other sister.

say: A human man at our door. The Nation sends men like you.
Where are you from, and who sent you? Neat answers get you nowhere.
We've been burned by smiles before.
Walk slow and keep your hands where I see them. Spies learn patience, and so do we.
Not one of the Flotsam ninjas, and not one of the Nation's. So what are you?
I have a long memory for faces. Give me a reason to forget yours.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE / DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), untested. Lore basis: refugees afraid of Holy Nation spies, ninjas calling each other sister.

say: Whose are the women? If they're yours, we'll be watching. If they aren't, we'll be asking them.
A man leading women. You may be a rescuer or a keeper. I can't tell yet.
Careful. If any of them wants to leave you, we won't stand in the way.
The Nation's men like to bring their women to heel. Show me you aren't that.
Keep your hands off them while you are here. I will not repeat myself.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE / DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), untested. Lore basis: refugees afraid of Holy Nation spies, ninjas calling each other sister.

say: Our sister returns. The door is yours.
Good to see you again. Come in off the road.
You have earned a place at the fire. Don't tell the Nation where it is.
We remember who helped. Sit and rest.
Nothing to prove to us. Not any more.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE / DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), untested. Lore basis: refugees afraid of Holy Nation spies, ninjas calling each other sister.

say: You earned the gate. You haven't earned the rest of the town.
A friend, and still a man. Forgive us. We have reasons to be careful.
We vouch for you. Don't make us regret it.
The ninjas say you're all right. I say it too, loosely.
Pass. And don't ask where we sleep.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE / DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), untested. Lore basis: refugees afraid of Holy Nation spies, ninjas calling each other sister.

say: Are you running too? Keep low. The Nation looks east first.
I thought you were one of them. Forgive me, women look the same when they are frightened.
Please, don't tell anyone you saw me. I'm only passing.
There's food, if you can find it, and ninjas, if you can't. Stay out of the middle.
I have not said a word, lady. I have learned not to.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_IS_FEMALE / DC_MIXED_GENDER_GROUP (target), untested. Lore basis: refugees afraid of Holy Nation spies, ninjas calling each other sister.

say: Swear on whatever you hold sacred that you aren't from the Nation.
Are you here for me? Say it plainly. I'd rather know.
Don't step closer. Please. I've had enough of men with kind faces.
The ninjas say we're safe. I believe it on alternate days.
I have nothing for you. No money, no secrets. Walk on.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: Don't even think of offering. I have turned down fatter purses than yours and written down the names.
That bag is a matter for the ledger, not for the pocket. I won't be paid to forget.
I have an honest face and a report waiting for any hand that tries to feed it.
Offer me a bribe and the fine doubles. Offer me nothing and it merely stays the same.
I took an oath. It isn't for sale, even to someone with a good story.
Close the bag. If you reach for the purse instead, I reach for the manacles.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: Whatever is in that pack, I'm not afraid of it, or of you. Reach for coin and I'll take you in.
I fear no one on this road. A bribe is only an insult that costs more.
Try me. I like a challenge, and the cells need filling.
I don't need your cats. I need a reason to draw this.
Bribery is a trade for cowards. I'm not one of them.
Many have tried. Most are still in the cells.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: Hm. A heavy pack, and a lighter purse than you pretend. A man could be reasonable, with the right figure.
Customs is a long job. A man gets tired. A man gets thirsty. You see how it is.
I have never seen that bag. I'd hate to start seeing it now.
A few cats make the eyes tired.
The Cities pay by the month. The rest I collect as I go.
Walk by slowly. Think about what it's worth to you.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: Th-that bag. Is it what I think it is? I'd rather not know. I'd rather you were somewhere else.
I'm only a guard. A small one. Whatever is in there, I didn't see it.
Please keep it closed. If the sergeant sees, we're both done. You more than me, I hope.
I do not want trouble. Nobody wants trouble. Maybe you have something to ease the trouble.
My hands are shaking. That's only the cold.
Keep moving, quietly. And if you have anything to say, say it quietly, too.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: Bribery is a sin before it's a crime. Keep your cats, and keep your hands from your purse.
The Flame cannot be bought. I have met men who tried.
You insult the faith and me. Reach for coin once more and I'll call it heresy.
Coin buys bread. It does not buy a paladin.
My honour is not a market stall. Open your pack, or be taken.
Confess what you carry before you offer to hide it.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: I do not fear your pack, or its darkness. Show me, or I will take it.
Darkness hides in bags and in bribes.
Cast it into the fire, or I cast you.
Try to buy me, heretic. Let us see how much it costs you.
I walk the line between the Flame and the dark every day. You won't push me over.
A coward takes coin. I'm not one.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: The faith is strong. The pay is not. A tithe might lighten my duty.
Heresy is heavy, and so is my list of duties. Perhaps a little lighter, hm?
I have seen nothing in that bag. The Flame does not ask me to look so hard.
A donation to the temple is always welcome. I'm the temple, today.
The High Paladin counts the faithful. He doesn't count the cats.
Walk slowly. Think of a generous number.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: The High Paladin has ordered stricter checks. If I miss one thing, I burn. Please. Do not make me look.
I am only a servant of the Flame. Whatever you carry, I wish I did not know.
If the Inquisitors find out I looked away, I will be the one in the cage.
Quietly, stranger. Whatever you decide, quietly.
My duty frightens me more than you do. Make it simple for us both.
Do not tempt me. I am a weak man, and the Flame sees weakness.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: Everything has a price here. Yours is probably in your pocket.
Paperwork is cheap. Silence costs a little more.
I'm paid to look at the goods. Not paid enough to look hard.
Hashish. Nice. The boss doesn't need to hear about it, does he?
Slow walk. Think about the number.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: The boss counts everything. If a crate goes missing it's my neck. Don't make me a thief as well.
Whatever that is, put it away. I didn't see it.
If they catch me looking away I'm on the block myself. Please.
I should search you. I want to go home in one piece more.
Quietly. Whatever you decide, quietly.

dialogues.note: Voice only; the bribe itself is vanilla's (Drug bust bribe and the gate dialogues, which already branch on DC_PERSONALITY_TAG). Depends on DC_HAS_ILLEGAL_ITEM (target) and the speaker personality tag.

say: Greed does not live long in Shek land. Take your hand from your purse, flatskin.
A Shek isn't paid to look away. Don't make the offer. You won't like the answer.
You carry weakness in a sack and insult in a hand. Both stay where I can see them.
I don't trade honour. Not for cats, not for anything you own.
Keep your coin, flatskin. The Shek have no place to put it.

dialogues.note: Gossip around the vanilla bribe mechanic; no condition beyond the bar. Cities factions are not required, any bar speaker.

say: A gate sergeant took a smuggler's purse and waved him in. The smuggler came back with friends. The sergeant doesn't stand at that gate now.
People say the Cities guards have a price. They say it sadly, as if it were weather.
Slip a tired guard a few cats and he forgets how to read. Slip it to a rested one and you forget how to walk.
A man bribed his way in at one gate and got robbed at the next. Nobody sold him a map of honest ones.
Two thousand for a patrol to look away. A few hundred for a sergeant at a gate. Cheap, until it isn't.

dialogues.note: Gossip around the vanilla bribe mechanic; no condition beyond the bar.

say: A gate guard turned in his own captain for taking coin. They made him sergeant, then posted him somewhere worse.
Some Cities guards cannot be bought. They are the ones who get posted to the dull towns.
I offered a patrolman a purse. He wrote my name down and asked me to spell it. I don't go to that gate now.
There's an honest guard at the south gate. Nobody has found his price. Several have gone broke looking.
A bribe is a gamble. Half the guards eat it. The other half eat you.

dialogues.note: Gossip around the vanilla bribe mechanic; no condition beyond the bar.

say: A paladin took a tithe to forget a pack. They say he was the one who turned my cousin in a month later.
The Flame can't be bought. A paladin on a bad month can be rented.
There are frightened men in the Nation's helmets. Frightened men look at the floor, if you ask them to.
A priest once let a smuggler pass for a donation. The temple got the cats. The priest got a cell.
Paladins are paid in prayer. Prayer doesn't buy bread.

dialogues.note: Gossip around the vanilla bribe mechanic; no condition beyond the bar.

say: A man tried to buy his way past a paladin in the city. They burned the bag. They didn't stop at the bag.
The holy ones despise bribes. Not the ones who offer, the ones who accept.
I would sooner swim the swamp than hand a Nation guard a coin.
Try buying a paladin and learn the colour of a cage.
Don't offer. In the Nation, offering is the crime they were waiting for.

dialogues.note: Gossip around the vanilla bribe mechanic; no condition beyond the bar.

say: Offer a Shek a bribe and learn what a flatskin's hand is worth. It isn't much, in pieces.
The Shek don't take coin to look away. Take it as a warning, not as a rumour.
I saw a flatskin try to bribe a Shek gate guard. He's still on his knees. He's very polite now.
A Shek called bribery the worst of crimes. He didn't say what was the second worst.
Strange kingdom. No tolls, no bribes. Only the blade, and then the apology.

dialogues.note: Gossip around the vanilla bribe mechanic; no condition beyond the bar.

say: Two thousand to look away at a patrol. A few hundred at a gate. Fifty if the guard is lazy and the night is long.
A guard takes your money depending on his mood. You don't learn his mood until you try.
Honest guards cost you nothing, and so much more. Crooked guards cost you cats, and still might not do it.
Never bribe the nervous ones in front of the sergeant. Nervous ones remember the sergeant.
Some take it. Some report you. Some do both, in that order.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: No pack. Good. A toll, paid in cats, and you walk. It's a fair price for walking.
You carry nothing worth the trouble. Give us a toll and we forget you were here.
Light on your feet and light in your hands. A toll. Hand it over and move.
Empty back. Then it's in your pockets. A toll, and we don't check.
Toll road. Cats. You don't even have a pack to complain about.
No bags to rob, so we take it in coin.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: Look at that pack. You are hiding more than you say. Pay, and then pay again.
A pack that size and you want to haggle? Empty it.
Nobody walks with a pack that heavy and nothing in it. How much is in there?
The toll is higher for the ones who carry. Take off the pack, or take out the cats.
A pack. That doubles the price, and halves my patience.
You tell me you have only a little, with that on your back? I don't believe you.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: Bags upon bags. A caravan on two legs! We shall be rich, or you'll be dead.
That's a lot of backpacks. Hand some over and we part friends.
I count three. Four. Where did you put the rest? Hand it over.
All that weight and not one cat to spare? Show me.
A walking warehouse. The toll just went up, and so did my appetite.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: No pack. Then you pay in cats or in blood.
Nothing on your back. The Reavers don't mind. You pay with what you have.
Little to take. Little to lose. A few hundred cats should do for the trouble.
Empty-backed and brave. Pay the toll, brave one.
You pass if you pay. We don't forgive. We don't forget, either.
No bags. Then the cats come from your belt.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: That pack is a lie waiting to be told. Open it or pay twice.
You carry something. We'll have our share of it.
Nobody lugs a pack that heavy for fun. Hand it over.
We cut open the heavy ones first.
A pack means cats. A pack means more cats than you say.
Show us your bag, stranger, or we'll find our own way inside.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: I count your packs and I do not like the number. Too many for one back, too few for a lie.
You're carrying a market. Share some of the market.
Every pack is a debt. You owe us for each.
That much weight. We would be fools to let it walk by.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: No pack on you. A toll, then, a small one, paid fast.
Walking light is wise. Walking free costs a few hundred cats.
Empty back, but you came this way for a reason.
Nothing to carry, nothing to hide. Pay what a poor traveller pays.
A few hundred cats and the road is yours.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: That backpack says you have more than a poor traveller. Pay as a rich one.
Weight like that's cats in disguise. Settle the toll.
A pack. Open it, or the price opens it for us.
You carry a lot to be so quiet. What's in it?
Don't tell me it's empty.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: Heavy-laden and slow. A target, and a gift.
More packs than shoulders. We shall relieve you of a few.
You are travelling with a shop. We are tax collectors.
Overloaded. That isn't a traveller, that's a donation.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: No pack? Nothing to eat in it. Cats then!
No bag, no food. Cats! Give us cats!
Empty back. Hmm. Pockets then. Pockets!
You got no food on you? Then pay. Pay with something.
Nothing to carry? Then something in your hands.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: A pack! Food in there, yes? Give!
That bag. What's in the bag? Food? Give us a little.
Heavy pack, heavy with food. Share. Please.
We won't hurt you. Give us the pack.
Open the bag. Show us. We only want to look. Then to eat.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: Nothing on your back, nothing to lose. This will be quick.
No pack, no tears. Just a body to pick over.
Empty-backed and unlucky. Cats first, then the rest.
Nobody comes this far with nothing unless they are running. Run, then.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: Fat pack. Fat purse. Good!
That backpack is for us. The rest of you can go with it.
Heavy bag and a heavier mistake.
You should have paid when we asked nicely. We were never that nice.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: No pack. We'll take it from the corpse.
Not worth the rope. Quick death, then.
Nothing on your back. Then the rest of you'll do.
Walk with nothing and die with nothing.

dialogues.note: Depends on DC_NUM_BACKPACKS (target): value 0, or more than 0 / 2. Untested in game. Barks only; the toll itself is vanilla's.

say: Fat pack. Cut it from the dead.
You carry well, stranger. You will carry for us.
Heavy bag, heavy loss for you. Take it!
The sea gives, and so do fools.

dialogues.note: Rumour about the vanilla toll talk; no condition.

say: They ask for coin if you carry nothing. They ask for everything if you carry a pack.
The Dust Bandits count your backpacks before they count your cats. A bag is an admission.
Three hundred is an insult to a bandit with a good eye. They know what a pack can hide.
Carry the bag, lose the bag. Leave it behind, lose a few hundred.
Bandits aren't stupid. A big pack and a small purse tells them a story, and they don't like the ending.

dialogues.note: Rumour about the vanilla toll talk; no condition.

say: Reavers charge by how heavy you look. I walked the coast with nothing on my back once. It cost me my boots.
The Reavers never take the first offer. They take the second, and the third, until there is no fourth.
Pay the road gangs early and light. Let them think you're poor. They won't believe you, but they'll remember the courtesy.
Pay the road gangs early and light. They won't believe you're poor, but they remember the courtesy.

dialogues.note: Rumour about the vanilla toll talk; no condition.

say: The hungry ones ask for food first. Cats when they have no food to ask for. Nothing when they have neither.
A man with no pack told a starving bandit he had nothing. They shared a long silence and parted friends.
Starvers don't set tolls. They set a mood. Meet it, and keep walking.
Never joke with a hungry bandit about your lunch. Only one of you'll be laughing, and it won't be him.

dialogues.note: Gossip only; no condition beyond the bar and, where stated, in_town_of. Lore basis: women without a male escort are punished; the Nation restricts women.

say: A woman out without her husband or brother gets noticed here. Noticed is the best you can hope for.
They restrict the women here. You get used to it. You stop noticing the quiet.
The priests say women are Narko's image. The priests are men. Make of that what you will.
Rumour has it a woman walked into the temple unescorted last month. She isn't mentioned any more.
Stay in, stay veiled, stay quiet. It's simpler than the alternative.

dialogues.note: Gossip only; no condition beyond the bar and, where stated, in_town_of. Lore basis: women without a male escort are punished; the Nation restricts women.

say: I've heard of women purged for stepping out without an escort. I've never asked what happened to the escort.
A woman's best protection here's a man who doesn't mind answering for her.
The Inquisitors check women first. That's how they find the tainted ones, people say.
If you must walk with a woman, stay close, speak first, and hope she says nothing.

dialogues.note: Gossip only; no condition beyond the bar and, where stated, in_town_of. Lore basis: women without a male escort are punished; the Nation restricts women.

say: Never take a woman north without a man beside her. The Nation doesn't ask questions. It doesn't need to.
A friend went into the Holy Nation with her husband. She came back. He didn't. That's how they do it.
I heard in the Nation a woman is punished for walking alone. They're right.
The Holy Nation punishes women who travel without a male escort. Most only fear it.

dialogues.note: Gossip only; no condition beyond the bar and, where stated, in_town_of. Lore basis: women without a male escort are punished; the Nation restricts women.

say: The Nation despises women who read, women who fight, and women who walk unescorted.
If you're a woman, and you must pass through the Holy Nation, find a man, or find another road.
I heard women flee the Nation for Flotsam. Not many reach it.
A woman in the Nation is a guest of whoever claims her. Claim yourself first, and walk away.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). say: Fallen out with the Anti-Slavers? There's a pacifier in Mud Town. Bring a great many cats.
Mud Town is where you buy the Anti-Slavers back.
The man in Mud Town can talk the Anti-Slavers round. Your purse does the real talking.
Mud Town sells forgiveness for the Anti-Slavers. Dear, but cheaper than a cage.
They say the Anti-Slavers' peacemaker sits in Mud Town. They are usually right about the price.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom, Tech Hunters, Swampers, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers, Mongrel

say: The Hounds hold grudges. The Hub holds a pacifier for them.
Wronged the Hounds? Go to the Hub and pay someone who talks gently.
There's a man in the Hub who makes the Hounds forget. For a fee.
Hounds don't forgive. Hounds are paid to. The Hub is where.
The Hub has a pacifier for the Hounds. It's on the same street as the people who need one.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation Outlaws, Swampers, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers, Mongrel

say: The Shek have a pacifier at World's End. It costs less than your head.
Cross the Shek? World's End has someone who mends that. Bring cats, not excuses.
They say a flatskin can buy peace with the Shek in World's End. A Shek would never say so.
World's End. The Shek peace is sold there. Strange, for a people with no use for coin.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation Outlaws, Tech Hunters, Swampers, Anti-Slavers, Mongrel

say: The slavers keep a pacifier at Stoat. Odd to pay slavers for peace. Odder not to.
If the slavers want you, Stoat has a man who talks them out of it.
Pay the slave traders at Stoat and they forget your face. They never forget the price.
Stoat. That's where the slavers mend their quarrels.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation Outlaws, Swampers, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers, Mongrel

say: The Cities angry at you? Flats Lagoon has a pacifier. Pay the fee, forget the fines.
Flats Lagoon will clear your name with the Cities. A very long ledger, a very short list of ways.
If the Empire wants you, go to Flats Lagoon with a heavy purse.
A man in Flats Lagoon sells you back to the Cities. Think of it as a loan.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names.

say: A pacifier costs a fortune. A bounty costs your head.
There is a man for every faction who will fix a bad name. They all want paying. Heavily.
The pacifier does not care who you killed. Only that you can pay for forgetting.
I saved for years to be forgiven. I spent it in one afternoon. I'd do it again.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names.

say: Pay the Nation for peace? Repentance is the only coin the Flame takes.
No man sells forgiveness here. Forgiveness is paid in prayer, and in ash.
A bounty with the Nation is settled in the cells or on the pyre. Nobody has found a third way.
The Nation forgives the penitent. The penitent don't come back to ask the price.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: Holy Nation Outlaws, Tech Hunters, Swampers, Mongrel, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers

say: The Shinobi keep a hut in most big towns. Heng, Catun, Heft. Ask for a quiet man.
Looking for the thieves? They keep a place in the larger towns. Heng has one, I'm told.
Join the Shinobi and the guards stop being your problem. Mostly.
Catun, Heft, Heng. Every one has a back door with nobody guarding it.
Thieves don't advertise. Look for the place the guards avoid looking at.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: Holy Nation Outlaws, Tech Hunters, Swampers, Mongrel, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers

say: The Shinobi sell membership like a stall sells bread.
They take cats at the door. Plenty of them. After that, you're a brother.
Thieves stick together. That costs more than sticking alone.
Joining the Shinobi costs a great deal. Not joining costs your pockets, now and then.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. Refusal by culture: Empire.

say: Thieves? There are no thieves in the Cities. Ask somebody else, and ask quietly.
I would never point a stranger toward that sort of place. I would not know where it was, either.
The Empire's law has an answer for people who ask. You won't like it.
Go and ask the guards. I'm sure they'll be curious why you want to know.
No. And I didn't hear the question.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. Refusal by culture: Holy Nation.

say: A den of sinners. I wouldn't name it, and I'll report whoever does.
Seek the thieves and the Flame will find you first.
There's no such place in Okran's land. If there were, I'd burn it.
Ask me that again and the Inquisitors will ask you why.
Pray for your own sake that you didn't mean what you said.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. Refusal by culture: Shek (race Shek, any bar).

say: Flatskin thieves and their holes. A Shek has no use for either.
Ask a flatskin. I don't keep company with shadows.
A thief is a coward with quick hands. I won't tell you where to find them.
No. A Shek doesn't lead anyone to a thieves' nest.
Go and ask the rats. They know.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: United Cities, Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation Outlaws, Tech Hunters, Swampers, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers, Mongrel

say: Black Desert City has the best robot limbs in the land. Taken off dead Skeletons, I hear.
Need a new leg? Black Desert City. Mind the sand, mind the twisters, mind your boots.
The Skeletons sell parts in Black Desert City. Used parts. Very used.
The robotics shop in Black Desert City is the best anywhere. The road there's the price.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: United Cities, Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation Outlaws, Tech Hunters, Swampers, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers

say: Mongrel sells robot legs. Plenty of demand. Mind the fog on the way.
Legs in Mongrel. Everyone there seems to need them. Do not ask why.
For a limb that works, go to Mongrel. For a limb that fits, bring patience.
Mongrel is where legs go when they've lost their owners. Cheap enough, if you can stand the fog.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: United Cities, Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation Outlaws, Tech Hunters, Swampers, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers, Mongrel

say: The Hivers sell cheap legs. Cheap, I said.
Need a leg and short of cats? The hive will sell you one. It won't look good.
A hive limb gets you walking. It does not get you admired.
The hive grows its own. It will sell you spares. Don't ask what they're made of.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. Refusal by culture: Holy Nation.

say: Machine limbs are an abomination. I won't tell you where to buy one. Wear one here, and you'll burn.
Ask about iron legs in the Nation and see how the street empties.
Cut off by the Skeleton wars and fitted with metal? Don't come here.
There's an iron foot in a ditch outside the walls. Its owner was found nearby.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names.

say: Parts come from the Black Desert, or from Mongrel. Or from whatever stops moving first.
I need a limb. A limb needs a donor. Donors are scarce, and often unwilling.
Spare parts are spare. Most of mine were somebody's.
A limb is a limb. Whose it was isn't my concern.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names.

say: Hurt? Any big town has someone with a needle and a bottle. Ask the barman, he has stitches of his own.
A doctor is easy to find. A good one is easy to afford, or neither.
Skeletons need robot repair, the rest of us need a doctor. The doctor is easier to find.
If you bleed in a town, someone will sew you up. If you bleed outside, bleed quietly.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation Outlaws, Tech Hunters, Swampers, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers, Mongrel

say: Catun has the most famous weapon smith. Heng has one of the best shops around. Both are worth the walk.
A good blade is from Catun. A better argument is from Heng. Take your pick.
For weapons, Catun and Heng. For anything else, the nearest gutter.
A Catun blade is good. A Heng blade is better. A blade from neither is a rumour.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: United Cities, Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation Outlaws, Tech Hunters, Swampers, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers, Mongrel

say: The Scraphouse in Black Desert City beats every weapon shop in the land. Getting there's the real test.
Best weapons are in Black Desert City. Worst road in the world to carry them back along.
A Scraphouse blade is a rumour I trust. I've seen what's left of the ones who bought one.
Scraphouse. Say the word and watch a tinker go quiet.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation Outlaws, Tech Hunters, Swampers, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers, Mongrel

say: Heft is the best place I found for armour. I cannot think of any other, unless you count the rumour about the Armour King.
Good plate comes from Heft. Everything else is a story.
If you want to stay alive, buy armour in Heft. If you want to stay in coins, don't.
Armour from Heft. Everything else I have bought has been a lesson.

dialogues.note: Service rumour; towns from the game data (Yara's pacifier directory and Hunter Edjack's shopping guide in vanilla books). Depends on in_town_of to avoid being said in the town it names. in_town_of: United Cities, Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation Outlaws, Swampers, Slave Traders, Anti-Slavers, The Holy Nation

say: For crossbows, the Tech Hunter towns. Mongrel too, if you don't mind the fog. Black Scratch is good.
The Tech Hunters make decent crossbows. They'll tell you so.
A crossbow out of Black Scratch has never failed me. I have never tested it on anything that fights back.
Heard Mongrel has a decent crossbow maker. Heard the fog has a better one.
